title: TerminologyAnalysis
description: Academic terminology refinement performed before bulk discovery: each seed keyword is audited, the product problem is translated into academic task families, and query families are built with an explicit DIRECT or TRANSFER role.
topic: reference resolution to propositions and the semantic scope of replies in work communication

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Reference by expressions such as this or that to a discourse segment or to an abstract object evoked by prior discourse rather than to an ordinary nominal entity.
seed_audit.main_risk: The antecedent may be modeled as a discourse segment or abstract discourse object rather than as the exact proposition span required by the product.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Purely theoretical deixis, spatial or temporal deixis, demonstratives referring to physical objects, and monologic discourse work with no computational antecedent resolution.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: A near-synonym of discourse deixis emphasizing the reference relation between a discourse-deictic expression and a prior discourse segment or discourse-evoked abstract entity.
seed_audit.main_risk: Terminology is less consistently indexed than discourse deixis or non-nominal-antecedent anaphora.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: General deixis, demonstrative semantics, discourse-segment theory without resolution, and physical-context reference.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Anaphoric reference whose antecedent is typically non-nominal and denotes or evokes an event, fact, proposition, situation, or other abstract discourse object.
seed_audit.main_risk: Some work assumes an anaphor or candidate antecedents are already identified and therefore does not solve end-to-end reference resolution.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Nominal shell-noun semantics without antecedent resolution, purely theoretical abstract-object semantics, and ordinary entity anaphora.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Anaphoric reference to proposition-like prior content, usually a subtype or interpretation of abstract or non-nominal-antecedent anaphora.
seed_audit.main_risk: The phrase is less standardized than abstract anaphora or non-nominal-antecedent anaphora and can miss relevant work indexed under broader terminology.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Formal-semantic discussions of propositions, propositional attitude anaphora, ellipsis, and logic papers without computational antecedent localization.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Anaphoric reference to a previously introduced event or eventuality.
seed_audit.main_risk: Searches easily drift into event coreference, temporal relation extraction, or event extraction rather than reference by a response expression to prior content.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Event extraction, event detection, temporal anaphora, event coreference clustering, and event schema induction.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: The broad task of identifying antecedents for anaphoric expressions.
seed_audit.main_risk: Most of the literature concerns nominal pronouns or entity antecedents rather than propositions, events, or discourse segments.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Pronoun resolution, nominal anaphora, zero anaphora, one-anaphora, entity identity, and language-specific syntactic anaphora.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Detection and clustering or linking of mentions that refer to the same discourse or real-world entity.
seed_audit.main_risk: Mainstream coreference overwhelmingly targets entity identity and does not represent a response semantically applying to a proposition.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Named-entity coreference, pronoun coreference, mention clustering, cross-document entity coreference, and entity linking.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Event coreference resolution: deciding whether two event mentions denote the same event and often clustering them.
seed_audit.main_risk: Identity between two event mentions is different from resolving an expression such as that, yes, approved, or not that part to an event antecedent.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Within-document and cross-document event clustering, news event matching, event nugget coreference, and event deduplication.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: A plausible descriptive label for reference to proposition-like content, but not a dominant standardized task name; the literature more often uses abstract anaphora, discourse deixis, or non-nominal antecedents.
seed_audit.main_risk: Literal searches may have low recall and may retrieve formal semantics rather than computational resolution.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Propositional identity in logic, semantic equivalence, proposition alignment, and philosophical discussions of propositions.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Coreference or anaphora resolution in dialogue or conversational data, potentially including identity, bridging, and discourse-deictic reference.
seed_audit.main_risk: The phrase often means ordinary entity coreference adapted to dialogue.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Speaker-aware entity coreference, pronoun resolution in chat, personal-reference resolution, and dialogue entity tracking.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: An umbrella description for resolving referring expressions in dialogue, including entities, discourse deixis, bridging, and sometimes situated or multimodal reference.
seed_audit.main_risk: The umbrella is too broad to guarantee propositional or response-scope resolution.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Visual reference resolution, referring-expression grounding to objects, entity reference in task-oriented dialogue, and multimodal deixis.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Recovering discourse structure in dialogue by predicting attachment links between discourse units and often classifying the discourse relation on each link.
seed_audit.main_risk: Many benchmarks attach whole elementary discourse units rather than locating the exact sub-proposition affected by a response.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Parsers evaluated only on coarse utterance links, models given gold links that only classify relation labels, and monologic discourse parsing.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Semantic or pragmatic relations between conversational contributions, such as question-answer pair, acknowledgement, correction, clarification, elaboration, or contrast.
seed_audit.main_risk: Recognizing a relation type is insufficient when the target span or attachment is supplied rather than predicted.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Relation-label classification over gold argument pairs and generic text discourse relations with no dialogue response attachment.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Identification or classification of rhetorical or discourse relations between discourse units.
seed_audit.main_risk: A large body of RST and PDTB work concerns monologic text and assumes relation arguments or adjacent spans rather than finding what a reply addresses.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: PDTB connective classification, RST relation classification, implicit discourse relation classification over supplied sentence pairs, and relation labeling without attachment prediction.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: A descriptive label for structural or semantic relations linking a response to an earlier contribution; neighboring standardized terms include reply-to structure, discourse attachment, question-answer pair, acknowledgement, and correction.
seed_audit.main_risk: The exact phrase is not a stable canonical task name and may miss the relevant dialogue-discourse literature.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Message threading based only on metadata, social-media reply graphs, response prediction, and response generation.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: A conversation-analysis concept for paired social actions such as question-answer, greeting-greeting, offer-acceptance, or request-response, generally produced by different turns.
seed_audit.main_risk: Adjacency pairing captures sequential organization but does not by itself determine exact semantic scope or proposition-level attachment.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Turn-taking studies, sociological conversation analysis without computational resolution, speech-recognition language modeling, and generic dialogue sequencing.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Classification or modeling of the communicative function of an utterance, such as question, answer, request, acknowledgement, agreement, or rejection.
seed_audit.main_risk: A dialogue-act label describes what the current utterance does but commonly omits which earlier proposition it applies to.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Standalone dialogue-act classification, intent classification, speech-act recognition without relational arguments, and Topic 05 action or request extraction.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: A descriptive term for pairing questions with their answers; related literatures use question-answer pair relations, answer selection, response selection, or discourse attachment.
seed_audit.main_risk: Searches often retrieve QA matching where a question is supplied explicitly instead of selecting among multiple prior questions.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: FAQ retrieval, answer sentence selection, open-domain QA, semantic similarity between questions and answers, and pre-aligned QA datasets.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: In formal semantics and dialogue theory, resolving a question concerns providing information that settles or partially settles it; the phrase can also refer to computational QA or ambiguity resolution.
seed_audit.main_risk: The phrase is highly ambiguous and requires answerhood, dialogue, or Questions Under Discussion constraints.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Question answering generally, ambiguous-question clarification, query reformulation, question generation, and issue resolution outside linguistic dialogue.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: A useful product description for which part of a question or set of questions an answer addresses, but not a widely standardized standalone NLP task name.
seed_audit.main_risk: Literal searches preferentially retrieve answer-span extraction or syntactic scope rather than semantic response scope.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Extractive QA answer spans, semantic-role scope, negation scope, and answer-length or answer-boundary studies.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Determining whether a response supplies only part of the information needed to resolve a question; partial answerhood is well established in formal question semantics, while a standalone computational detection task is less standardized.
seed_audit.main_risk: Computational search results may be sparse or may confuse partial correctness with partial semantic answerhood.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Partially correct student answers, answer grading, incomplete QA generation, extractive span truncation, and factuality scoring.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Systems that process or answer more than one question in conversational or multi-question settings.
seed_audit.main_risk: Most such systems generate answers to multiple supplied questions rather than infer which subset of earlier questions a single human reply addresses.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Multi-question QA, batch QA, conversational QA with one current question, VQA with multiple questions, and question generation.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Classifying whether a conversational contribution expresses agreement, often versus disagreement or neutrality.
seed_audit.main_risk: Many datasets classify the response as agreeing without requiring identification of the exact proposition or span agreed with.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Message-level polarity classification, sentiment analysis, stance with a fixed topic, and agreement labels with gold reply links.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Classifying whether a contribution expresses disagreement, dispute, contradiction, or correction relative to prior content.
seed_audit.main_risk: A disagreement label may not expose the proposition being rejected and can conflate disagreement with negative sentiment.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Sentiment polarity, toxicity, argument mining without target links, contradiction classification over supplied pairs, and fixed-thread disagreement labels.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Identification of the prior content toward which agreement is directed; the capability is directly relevant although the exact phrase is not a dominant standardized task label.
seed_audit.main_risk: Relevant work may instead be indexed under discourse attachment, target-specific stance, acknowledgement relations, public commitments, or argument-target relations.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Agreement classification with a gold target, stance toward named entities or topics, and social-media target extraction unrelated to propositions.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: The semantic content over which an agreement or acknowledgement holds, including the possibility of partial agreement; the concept occurs in dialogue semantics even though the phrase itself is not a standardized computational benchmark name.
seed_audit.main_risk: Literal searches have limited recall and can retrieve legal, organizational, or contract-scope material.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Contractual agreement scope, inter-annotator agreement scope, organizational consensus, and generic agreement detection with no target localization.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Joint or staged identification of a target and the stance expressed toward it, usually favor, oppose, or neutral.
seed_audit.main_risk: Typical stance targets are entities, claims, topics, or authors rather than exact antecedent propositions in a dialogue.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Topic-level stance classification, political stance toward named targets, sentiment-target extraction, and aspect sentiment analysis.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Testing whether one text entails another proposition; this corresponds to textual entailment or natural language inference when the proposition is supplied.
seed_audit.main_risk: NLI evaluates the relation after the candidate proposition is already given and therefore does not solve antecedent selection or response scope.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Generic NLI benchmarks, textual entailment over arbitrary sentence pairs, semantic textual similarity, and claim verification without conversational attachment.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Detection of semantic incompatibility between two propositions, commonly as one label in natural language inference.
seed_audit.main_risk: The compared proposition is normally supplied, so contradiction detection alone cannot determine what part of a prior message the response rejects.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Generic NLI, fact checking, contradiction in summarization, knowledge-base inconsistency, and whole-document factuality.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: A target-domain or genre term rather than an academic task name.
seed_audit.main_risk: Used alone it retrieves communication studies, email classification, summarization, spam, threading, and writing assistance rather than reference resolution.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Spam detection, email intent classification, email summarization, response generation, writing style, organizational communication, and thread reconstruction.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: A structural and genre cue indicating a response message in asynchronous communication.
seed_audit.main_risk: Most email-reply work concerns threading, reply prediction, quote extraction, response generation, or latency rather than semantic scope.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Email thread reconstruction, quotation attribution, reply recommendation, response generation, reply-time prediction, and social-network analysis.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: A product-relevant description of which proposition, amount, date, clause, or option an approval applies to, but not a well-established standalone academic task label.
seed_audit.main_risk: Literal searches attract legal, workflow, permission, governance, and access-control uses of approval.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Access approvals, workflow authorization, legal approval processes, regulatory scope, and speech-act detection that only labels an utterance as an approval.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: A domain descriptor spanning email, enterprise chat, meetings, organizational discourse, and collaborative work.
seed_audit.main_risk: It is far too broad as a task term and should only constrain searches built around stronger reference or discourse terminology.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Organizational behavior, communication effectiveness, workplace sentiment, productivity, meeting analysis, social networks, and generic collaboration research.

task_families.name: Non-nominal antecedent anaphora and discourse deixis
task_families.description: Resolve anaphoric expressions to non-nominal antecedent spans that evoke events, facts, propositions, situations, or discourse segments; include anaphoricity and unresolved/no-supported-antecedent decisions where available.
task_families.why_it_matters: This is the closest established academic formulation of references such as this, that, that proposal, or not that part when the antecedent is propositional or eventive rather than an entity mention.
seed_papers: Bonnie Lynn Webber (1988), Discourse Deixis: Reference to Discourse Segments.
Nicholas Asher (1993), Reference to Abstract Objects in Discourse.
Ana Marasović, Leo Born, Juri Opitz, and Anette Frank (2017), A Mention-Ranking Model for Abstract Anaphora Resolution.
Varada Kolhatkar, Adam Roussel, Stefanie Dipper, and Heike Zinsmeister (2018), Survey: Anaphora With Non-nominal Antecedents in Computational Linguistics: a Survey.

task_families.name: Discourse deixis and anaphora resolution in dialogue
task_families.description: Resolve identity, bridging, and especially discourse-deictic or abstract anaphoric relations in conversational data, with discourse deixis treated separately from ordinary entity coreference.
task_families.why_it_matters: This family adds dialogue-specific turn structure, speakers, and conversational antecedent candidates to the non-nominal reference problem.
seed_papers: Sopan Khosla, Juntao Yu, Ramesh Manuvinakurike, Vincent Ng, Massimo Poesio, Michael Strube, and Carolyn Rosé (2021), The CODI-CRAC 2021 Shared Task on Anaphora, Bridging, and Discourse Deixis in Dialogue.
Shengjie Li, Hideo Kobayashi, and Vincent Ng (2021), The CODI-CRAC 2021 Shared Task on Anaphora, Bridging, and Discourse Deixis Resolution in Dialogue: A Cross-Team Analysis.

Juntao Yu, Sopan Khosla, Ramesh Manuvinakurike, Lori Levin, Vincent Ng, Massimo Poesio, Michael Strube, and Carolyn Rosé (2022), The CODI-CRAC 2022 Shared Task on Anaphora, Bridging, and Discourse Deixis in Dialogue.

task_families.name: Dialogue discourse attachment and relation parsing
task_families.description: Predict which previous discourse unit or complex discourse unit a reply attaches to and classify the semantic-pragmatic relation, including question-answer pair, acknowledgement, correction, clarification, conditional, contrast, and related response relations.
task_families.why_it_matters: A system that jointly predicts attachment and relation type provides a close structural approximation to response span → antecedent → relation, and dialogue corpora can contain non-adjacent and interleaved responses.
seed_papers: Nicholas Asher, Julie Hunter, Mathieu Morey, Farah Benamara, and Stergos Afantenos (2016), Discourse Structure and Dialogue Acts in Multiparty Dialogue: the STAC Corpus.

Jiaqi Li, Ming Liu, Min-Yen Kan, Zihao Zheng, Zekun Wang, Wenqiang Lei, Ting Liu, and Bing Qin (2020), Molweni: A Challenge Multiparty Dialogues-based Machine Reading Comprehension Dataset with Discourse Structure.
Yaxin Fan, Feng Jiang, Peifeng Li, Fang Kong, and Qiaoming Zhu (2023), Improving Dialogue Discourse Parsing via Reply-to Structures of Addressee Recognition.

task_families.name: Question-answer relations, Questions Under Discussion, and partial answerhood
task_families.description: Model whether a proposition answers a question, which question is under discussion, and whether an answer is complete, partial, indirect, or non-responsive; computational dialogue attachment work and formal answerhood semantics are both relevant.
task_families.why_it_matters: The product must distinguish a reply that resolves one prior question or only part of one question from a reply that resolves all outstanding questions.
seed_papers: Jeroen Groenendijk and Martin Stokhof (1984), foundational work on the semantics of questions, answers, and partial answers.
Jonathan Ginzburg (1995), Resolving Questions, I.
Nicholas Asher, Julie Hunter, Mathieu Morey, Farah Benamara, and Stergos Afantenos (2016), Discourse Structure and Dialogue Acts in Multiparty Dialogue: the STAC Corpus.

task_families.name: Agreement, disagreement, acknowledgement, correction, and public commitments
task_families.description: Model agreement or dispute relative to prior discourse commitments and identify the content affected by acknowledgement, correction, rejection, or partial agreement.
task_families.why_it_matters: This is the closest literature for yes, agreed, approved, no, not that part, and similar responses whose business meaning depends on the exact proposition accepted or rejected.
seed_papers: Alex Lascarides and Nicholas Asher (2008), Agreement and Disputes in Dialogue.
Alex Lascarides and Nicholas Asher (2009), Agreement, Disputes and Commitments in Dialogue.
Sara Rosenthal and Kathy McKeown (2015), I Couldn't Agree More: The Role of Conversational Structure in Agreement and Disagreement Detection in Online Discussions.

task_families.name: Event reference and event coreference
task_families.description: Resolve identity and anaphoricity among event mentions and use event representations, contextual arguments, and clustering evidence as transfer mechanisms for event-like antecedents.
task_families.why_it_matters: The product may refer back to an event or eventuality, but standard event coreference normally solves mention identity rather than response-to-event semantic scope.
seed_papers: Kevin Humphreys, Robert Gaizauskas, and Saliha Azzam (1997), Event coreference for information extraction.
Prafulla Kumar Choubey and Ruihong Huang (2017), Event Coreference Resolution by Iteratively Unfolding Inter-dependencies among Events.

task_families.name: Target-specific stance, entailment, and contradiction
task_families.description: Use target identification, proposition-pair inference, entailment, contradiction, and stance mechanisms after or jointly with antecedent selection.
task_families.why_it_matters: These methods may help determine whether a response supports, rejects, contradicts, or conditions a candidate proposition, but they do not by themselves find the correct candidate.
seed_papers: Sara Rosenthal and Kathy McKeown (2015), I Couldn't Agree More: The Role of Conversational Structure in Agreement and Disagreement Detection in Online Discussions.

task_families.name: Multiple- and split-antecedent reference
task_families.description: Resolve references whose interpretation depends on more than one antecedent span, using split-antecedent and multi-antecedent resolution methods as methodological transfer evidence.
task_families.why_it_matters: Responses such as do the first two or acknowledgements applying to several propositions require multi-span output, but mainstream split-antecedent work is usually about plural entity anaphora rather than propositions.
seed_papers: Juntao Yu, Nafise Sadat Moosavi, Silviu Paun, and Massimo Poesio (2021), Stay Together: A System for Single and Split-antecedent Anaphora Resolution.

task_families.name: Workplace and asynchronous message response grounding
task_families.description: Search specifically for proposition-level reference, discourse attachment, question-answer relations, agreement scope, and partial responses in email, enterprise chat, and other asynchronous work communication.
task_families.why_it_matters: Target-domain evidence is needed to determine whether methods developed on spoken dialogue, game chat, forums, or news transfer to business email and enterprise messaging; domain papers are only direct when they actually evaluate the required semantic capability.

demoted_terms: anaphora resolution when used without non-nominal or discourse constraints
event anaphora when used without reference or antecedent constraints
question resolution when used without answerhood or dialogue constraints
downgrade_rules: Downgrade or exclude entity-only coreference papers unless they separately evaluate non-nominal, event, proposition, situation, or discourse-deictic antecedents.

Downgrade event-coreference papers that only cluster event mentions referring to the same real-world event; admit them as TRANSFER unless they also resolve an anaphoric or response expression to an event antecedent.
Downgrade dialogue-act or speech-act classification when the model labels the current utterance but does not identify the antecedent proposition, discourse unit, or response target.
Downgrade discourse-relation classification if gold argument pairs, gold attachment links, or adjacent sentence pairs are supplied and the system never has to find what the response attaches to.

Downgrade monologic RST or PDTB relation work unless its mechanism or evaluation directly transfers to antecedent selection, argument-span identification, or uncertainty; ordinary implicit-relation classification is not sufficient.
Downgrade QA benchmarks in which the question is supplied as gold and the model only finds or generates an answer; this does not test which prior question a reply addresses.
Downgrade conversational QA that tracks a current user question but never selects among multiple outstanding prior questions.

Downgrade multi-question answering systems that answer several supplied questions in parallel; the required capability is mapping one observed response to the subset of earlier questions or propositions it actually resolves.
Downgrade partial-credit, student-answer grading, or partially correct QA literature unless partiality is defined semantically relative to the information requested by a question.
Downgrade agreement or disagreement classification that assigns one label to a whole message, comment, or reply while the agreement target is given or remains unlocalized.
Downgrade stance or sentiment papers whose target is only a named entity, author, hashtag, broad topic, or fixed claim and which cannot identify the exact target proposition or span.
Downgrade whole-message natural-language-inference, entailment, or contradiction systems when candidate proposition pairs are supplied and the system cannot locate the affected proposition itself.

Downgrade systems that force exactly one antecedent when the task permits several plausible antecedents, multiple antecedent spans, no supported antecedent, or genuine ambiguity, unless the paper supplies a transferable scoring or calibration method.

Downgrade email-thread reconstruction, quotation extraction, source attribution, header-based reply graphs, and subject-based conversation grouping; these are structural inputs from Topics 01 and 03, not Topic 04 semantic scope.
Downgrade email summarization, reply generation, response recommendation, and response-time prediction unless they explicitly evaluate antecedent or response-scope resolution.

Downgrade approval, request, commitment, or decision speech-act detection if it only identifies that an approval or commitment occurred but not what content it applies to; that capability belongs primarily to Topic 05 until scope is modeled.
Downgrade bridging-reference work that only resolves associative entity relations; dialogue bridging is adjacent but does not substitute for propositional or discourse-deictic reference.

Downgrade visual, table, cell, page, screenshot, and attachment grounding to Topic 08 unless the paper supplies a general reference-resolution mechanism useful to Topic 04, in which case label it TRANSFER.

Downgrade papers that evaluate only coarse whole-turn antecedents when the data contain multiple independent propositions inside a turn, unless the paper explicitly discusses sub-turn spans, elementary discourse units, complex discourse units, or argument scope.

Downgrade papers that report accuracy only on cases where a valid antecedent is guaranteed if the product needs unresolved or unsupported cases; prefer work that includes anaphoricity, no-link, unanswerable, abstention, or calibrated uncertainty.

Do not treat synthetic or non-workplace dialogue evidence as proof of business-email accuracy; it may support mechanisms or engineering experiments but remains transfer evidence for the production domain.

date_policy.rationale: Discovery must reach at least 1973 because adjacency-pair and sequential-response concepts come from foundational conversation analysis in the 1970s. For the more central semantic and computational branches, foundational work is also substantially older than modern neural NLP: formal work on questions and partial answers was established by the 1980s, Webber's computational treatment of discourse deixis appeared in 1988, and Asher's systematic treatment of reference to abstract objects appeared in 1993. A 2000-, 2010-, or transformer-era cutoff would therefore silently remove the conceptual foundations needed to interpret later task formulations correctly.
date_policy.operational_search_policy: Use 1973 as the hard canonical-foundation floor. Do not run every broad lexical query uniformly back to 1973: perform targeted foundational searches for adjacency pairs, question semantics/partial answerhood, discourse deixis, abstract-object anaphora, dialogue context, and public commitments; then use broader computational discovery from approximately the late 1990s onward. Modern benchmark and model searches should still extend through the current literature.
